hypothesis: Explicit Bayesian belief over verification regimes plus a priced Value of Diagnosis selects actions better than a one-line diagnostic heuristic.
evidence: 12 independent seeds, 6 design families, 20 obligations. G 1.256 +/- 0.000; H 1.291 +/- 0.038 (+2.7% relative). Pre-registered threshold 5%; H's worst run 1.229 fell below G's mean. Probing cost 1.00 -> 2.75.
reason: benefit +2.8% vs bar 11.5% (threshold 5% + uncertainty 3.0% + complexity 3.5%). The simpler policy already meets the requirement, so the additional machinery is not paid for by the evidence.
revisit_if: LONG-HORIZON boards: the best first action has low immediate value but unlocks later value, so a one-step expected-value rule cannot see the chain
COUPLED obligations: one action affects many properties at once, so per-obligation greedy choices can be globally poor
NON-STATIONARY environments: an RTL commit changes which channel pays, faster than a realised-rate heuristic re-learns
LARGE action spaces: thousands of candidate stimuli, assertions or decompositions, where a heuristic becomes too coarse to rank
MULTI-STEP diagnosis: probe -> interpret -> probe again, which requires reasoning about future information rather than one probe
complexity_note: ~3x probing spend; a belief model, sampler and VoD calculation to maintain and to keep correct.

hypothesis: A SEQUENCE of cheap real diagnostic actions (short Verilator run, then rtl_graph structural analysis) allocates verification effort better than a one-step diagnostic policy, on real RTL with real tools.
evidence: REAL tools, 12 seeds, 6 design families. G 0.998 +/-0.012, K 1.149 +/-0.031, realisable 1.324. Relative +15.0%, absolute 0.150 > 2x0.031, CI width 0.036. prereg sha256:618e564d5497168e INTACT.
reason: Met the committed rule. But the control never obtained structural information AT ALL, so this number confounds two things: acquiring real structural facts, and acquiring them conditionally. Experiment 9 was run to separate them and found 56% of the gain is the information alone. This record must not be cited as evidence for planning depth; cite Experiment 9 for that.
revisit_if: a regime appears where the chain must exceed depth 2
structural facts stop being obtainable by static reading
complexity_note: Four defects were found in the arm before this number was trusted: free structural facts (charged for what it already held, -52.6%); the branch was dead code behind a copied hasattr(self,'belief') guard while still reporting +39.2%; the step-2 gate used _uncertain(sig), false by construction after step 1; and hard->sim had no cap, the 162-sim-pass loop returning. Every one is now a permanent adversarial test.

hypothesis: The SEQUENCING earns Experiment 8's gain, rather than the mere acquisition of structural information.
evidence: REAL tools, 12 seeds, 6 design families. L 1.083 +/-0.000, K 1.149 +/-0.031. Sequencing alone +6.1%, absolute 0.066 vs a noise floor of 0.062 — a 6% margin. 56% of Experiment 8's gain is information, not sequencing. prereg sha256:d53c2aadc4d29c3b INTACT.
reason: The two rules disagree and the project should not pretend otherwise. The pre-registered rule returns MET (+6.1% > 5%). The promotion rule, which adds the measured spread to the bar, returns NOT MET (+6.1% vs 7.9%). Consistency also cuts toward K: its worst run (1.123) sits above L's mean (1.083), which is the same dominance argument used to REJECT H. The effect is real and small, and which way it falls depends entirely on how machinery is priced. Recording it as a clean win or a clean loss would both be false.
revisit_if: K beats L by >5% with the spread charged, on >=24 seeds
a regime requires a chain deeper than 2 steps
structure becomes expensive to obtain, making WHEN to buy it matter
complexity_note: Decisive for the actual question regardless of how this resolves: the chain that won is HAND-WRITTEN and two steps deep. Nothing here shows the chain must be LEARNED. A learned dynamics model is a far larger complexity jump than 6.1% of sequencing value can justify. DO NOT BUILD THE WORLD MODEL.

hypothesis: L-static-onestep (one structural read per OBLIGATION, no probe, no chain) should replace G-diagnostic as the default policy.
evidence: REAL tools, 24 seeds, 6 families. Full board L 1.083 vs G 0.998 (+8.5%, cleared the bar). HELD-OUT (lfsr, mv_filter) L 1.226 vs G 1.299 (-5.6%). prereg sha256:2158cdcd9a28fe05 INTACT.
reason: Failed committed side condition (2): worse on the designs it had never seen. I first read this as overfitting to the dev designs. That was WRONG, and the aggregate number could not have told me — only per-read instrumentation could. L paid 0.5 per OBLIGATION for a fact that belongs to a DESIGN: 6 of 11 reads redundant on the full board, 4 of 6 on held-out. The overhead amortises over 20 obligations and dominates over 7, which produced a win on the full board and a loss on the small split. A cost-model error and overfitting are indistinguishable from E alone.
revisit_if: never as specified — superseded by M-static-cached
complexity_note: Third appearance of ONE recurring defect: being charged for information already held. It cost Experiment 8 a -52.6% result, then hid inside L disguised as overfitting. Now a permanent test, plus an in-run instrument check.

hypothesis: M-static-cached (one structural read per DESIGN, no probe, no chain) should replace G-diagnostic as the default policy.
evidence: REAL tools, 24 seeds, 6 families. Full board M 1.120 +/-0.000 vs G 0.998 +/-0.012 (+12.2%, bar 6.2%, CI width 0.010). Held-out M 1.310 vs G 1.299 (+0.9%, NOT WORSE). Closed weight equal at 98.0. Zero redundant structural reads in the worst run. realisable 1.324. prereg sha256:03795d3516b2d507 INTACT.
reason: All four committed conditions held, including the held-out split that rejected L and the in-run instrument check confirming the diagnosed defect was actually fixed. RECOMMENDED changed from G-diagnostic to M-static-cached.
revisit_if: held-out margin fails to replicate on a corpus with >=3 held-out design families
a design appears whose structure is not statically readable
any future candidate beats M on held-out, not merely on the full board
complexity_note: M is the THIRD default candidate tested (H, L, M), and testing until something wins manufactures false positives. Mitigating: M is not a new hypothesis but L with a defect removed, diagnosed BEFORE the fix was written; and the held-out condition — the guard against exactly this — was re-committed unchanged and passed. NOT mitigated: the held-out margin is +0.9% across only 2 design families. The claim is 'better on the full board, not worse on held-out'. It is NOT 'better everywhere'.

hypothesis: REVISIT CONDITION DISCHARGED — 'MULTI-STEP diagnosis: probe -> interpret -> probe again' was recorded as a condition under which H-uncertainty (posteriors + priced Value-of-Diagnosis) should be reconsidered. Experiments 8 and 9 tested that regime directly.
evidence: Experiment 8: a real two-step chain (Verilator probe -> rtl_graph read) beat the one-step control by +15.0%. Experiment 9 ablated it: 56% of that was the INFORMATION, and sequencing alone was worth +6.1%, which failed the complexity-priced bar. No posterior and no VoD calculation was involved in the chain that won.
reason: The multi-step regime turned out to exist and to matter slightly, but it did not vindicate H. What paid in that regime was a hand-written two-step chain over real tool output, not sampled P(a is best) over a learned posterior. The condition is discharged WITHOUT reinstating H: a revisit trigger firing is permission to re-test, not a verdict.
revisit_if: a regime requires a chain deeper than 2 steps
a chain must be LEARNED rather than written, which is the only thing that would justify a dynamics model
complexity_note: Four of H's five revisit conditions remain open and untested: long-horizon boards, coupled obligations, non-stationarity, and large action spaces. The horizon and coupling results so far are SYNTHETIC/STRUCTURAL stress tests indicating substantial vulnerability of the current planner to long-horizon and coupled-obligation structure; real-tool validation remains pending.

hypothesis: COUPLED OBLIGATIONS EXIST AND ARE MEASURABLE. Experiments 6 and 7 DECLARED their dependency structure, which is why their +14.9% and +72.4% are synthetic structural stress tests. This probe declares nothing: it asks the solver whether proving one obligation makes a second one provable, on the real cv32e40p_fifo with yosys/z3.
evidence: REAL tools (SymbiYosys + z3, k-induction, depth 12) on the vendored cv32e40p_fifo. tap_control PASS (observation ports real). cnt_lemma PASS. state_match PASS standalone (pointers + count + memory). integrity_state PASS by k-induction GIVEN the lemma. integrity alone UNKNOWN (base case passes 12 steps, induction fails). integrity_lemma (cnt<=DEPTH assumed) UNKNOWN — identical failure. integrity_mut FAILS at step 7 (negative control armed).
reason: A genuine coupled-obligation structure, MEASURED rather than declared: a data-integrity property that is true but not inductive becomes provable once a state-matching lemma is proved first. Also a real negative result on the way: `cnt <= DEPTH` is sound, proves easily, and does NOT help — induction fails identically with and without it. The lemma that works relates the two machines' pointers, count AND memory. This is the ground Experiments 6/7 lacked.
revisit_if: a design appears whose lemma cannot be expressed over exposed state
the coupling structure must be DISCOVERED automatically rather than hand-written — that is the real Experiment 12
complexity_note: FIVE instrument defects found, every one of which made a broken instrument look green: (1) the model gated updates on testmode, which this FIFO never uses in its datapath; (2) it skipped flush cycles instead of mirroring them; (3) hierarchical references silently became UNDRIVEN wires in both yosys and sv2v, so the lemma was assumed against floating signals and constrained nothing; (4) the lemma task also asserted the property it supports, so it could never be proved — circular; (5) WORST: the reference model decided push acceptance from the DUT's own full_o, so it inherited the mutant's bug and the negative control detected nothing. (5) was invisible until (1) and (2) were fixed — each repair removed a spurious divergence until the control finally revealed it had never been checking. Fixed in the other order, this would have shipped a vacuous proof under a green negative control. All five are now permanent tests.

hypothesis: On a board carrying a MEASURED lemma dependency, ordering an obligation by what it UNLOCKS beats ordering by immediate utility.
evidence: REAL tools (SymbiYosys + z3) on the cv32e40p_fifo coupling board. M 1.167, N 1.400, +20.0%. Both close 28.0 weight. M wasted 12/12 direct proof attempts on fifo.integrity (inconclusive); N wasted 0. Action traces: M runs 6 formal actions (integrity, cnt_bound, no_overflow, flags, state_match, integrity), N runs 5 (state_match, integrity, cnt_bound, no_overflow, flags). prereg sha256:33efa91c898c31b5 INTACT.
reason: The dependency was MEASURED by the coupling probe, not declared: fifo.integrity is true but not inductive, and only becomes provable once fifo.state_match is proved. Both arms had identical channels, identical lemma-aware routing, and the same re-attempt rule, so the ONLY difference is order. The committed instrument check confirmed the coupling was exercised (12 inconclusive direct attempts).
revisit_if: a second design acquires a measured lemma dependency, which would allow a non-deterministic multi-family version of this test
the coupling structure must be DISCOVERED rather than hand-written
complexity_note: THE GAIN IS EXACT, NOT ESTIMATED, AND '12 SEEDS' IS NOT REPLICATION. The board is fully deterministic — every action is formal and memoised, neither ordering uses randomness — so 12 campaigns are 1 campaign repeated 12 times. M pays 24.0 (6 formal actions), N pays 20.0 (5); 24/20 = 1.20 exactly. The committed noise criterion (absolute > 2x std) is VACUOUS here. A related defect was found writing the warning: the determinism guard tested `std == 0.0`, but variance over 12 identical values returns 2.3e-16, so the guard never fired and the caveat stayed invisible — a silent check that reads as 'handled' in the source. Now detected by counting distinct outcomes. ALSO: one design family, below the usual three, because only the FIFO has a measured lemma dependency. This shows the mechanism is real; it does NOT show it generalises.

hypothesis: REVISIT CONDITION PARTIALLY DISCHARGED — 'COUPLED obligations' was recorded as a condition for reconsidering H-uncertainty.
evidence: Experiment 13 tested the coupled regime on a measured dependency. What paid was ORDERING by what an obligation unlocks (+20.0%, exact). No posterior, no sampled P(a is best), no priced VoD was involved.
reason: The coupled regime exists and matters, and it did NOT vindicate H. A one-line ordering rule captured the whole effect. Two of H's five revisit conditions are now discharged without reinstating it (multi-step diagnosis, coupled obligations); three remain untested: long-horizon boards, non-stationarity, and large action spaces.
revisit_if: long-horizon boards
non-stationary environments
large action spaces
complexity_note: Experiment 7's +72.4% for coupling-aware ordering STILL stands only as a synthetic structural stress test — its dependency was declared. Experiment 13 does not retroactively validate it; it replaces it on one design family.

hypothesis: The lemma dependency measured on the FIFO RECURS on a second, held-out design — i.e. it is a property of verification, not an artifact of one DUT or one invariant shape.
evidence: REAL tools (SymbiYosys + z3, k-induction, depth 24) on the pulp mv_filter, a HELD-OUT design no policy was developed against. mvf_tap PASS (tap wired). mvf_state PASS standalone (s_cnt == counter_q). mvf_equiv_lemma PASS by k-induction GIVEN the lemma. mvf_equiv UNKNOWN (base case passes 24 steps, induction fails). mvf_equiv_mut FAILS at step 13 (negative control armed).
reason: Two designs, two measured lemma dependencies, and the lemma SHAPES differ: the FIFO needed pointers + count + memory, mv_filter needs a single scalar counter. So the recurring thing is the phenomenon — a true-but-not-inductive property closed by a separately proved lemma — not one invariant that happened to work twice. This discharges the revisit condition recorded against Experiment 13 ('a second design acquires a measured lemma dependency').
revisit_if: a design is found whose dependent property is inductive alone, which would bound how common the phenomenon is
the coupling structure must be DISCOVERED automatically rather than hand-written — still the open problem
complexity_note: THE PROBE WORKED FIRST TRY, where the FIFO took six attempts. Nothing was smarter here; the five defects the FIFO probe exposed were applied as design rules up front — tap as a PORT (no hierarchical refs), a connectivity control read before anything else, the lemma asserted ALONE, the reference model reading only the DUT's INPUTS so it cannot inherit the mutation, and shadow storage reset to match the DUT. That is what the failure memory is FOR, and it is the first direct evidence that it transfers to new work rather than only preventing repeats. STILL TRUE: both boards are formal-only and therefore DETERMINISTIC, so seed counts on them remain repetition rather than replication.

hypothesis: Lemma-aware ordering generalises across design families carrying measured dependencies with DIFFERENT lemma shapes.
evidence: REAL tools, 2 design families, 12 campaigns. Both families: M 1.136, N 1.389 (+22.2%), closed weight equal at 50.0. HELD-OUT family alone (mv_filter): M 1.100, N 1.375 (+25.0%). Coupling exercised on BOTH families (12 inconclusive direct attempts each). prereg sha256:17d0923baca393f6 INTACT.
reason: All four committed conditions held, including the two written to stop overclaiming: the dependency had to be exercised on BOTH families (not a FIFO-driven win with extra obligations attached), and the effect had to survive on the held-out family considered alone. It did, and it was LARGER there (+25.0% vs +22.2%) — the opposite of the overfitting signature that rejected L-static-onestep in Experiment 10. This discharges Experiment 13's single-family caveat.
revisit_if: a board mixing simulation and formal makes this non-deterministic, which would let stability be measured rather than assumed
a third family with a measured dependency
the coupling structure must be DISCOVERED rather than hand-written
complexity_note: STILL DETERMINISTIC. Both boards are formal-only with no randomness in either ordering rule, so 12 campaigns remain 1 campaign repeated 12 times and the committed noise criterion is still vacuous. Two families answers GENERALISATION ACROSS DESIGNS; it does not answer STABILITY UNDER NOISE, and those are different questions. Experiment 7's +72.4% is NOT revived — its dependency was declared and it remains a structural stress test. What is promoted is a one-line ordering rule (value an obligation by what it unlocks), not a planner.

hypothesis: Wiring in mv_filter's real testbench makes the coupled board stochastic, so the determinism caveat on Experiments 13 and 14 can be discharged and their noise criterion made meaningful.
treatment: N-lemmafirst on a mixed sim+formal board
evidence: REAL tools, 24 seeds. Committed condition (1) — the campaigns must actually DIFFER — FAILED: 1 distinct outcome per arm, std 0.000, and the real numbers were byte-identical to mock. Direct check of the cause: SimRouter.run over seeds {1,7,42,999,31337} returns 'pass' for mvf.sticky on every seed and 'counterexample' for mvf.bug on every seed. prereg sha256:9f0816e89b5bc104 INTACT.
reason: NO VERDICT RECORDED, by the committed rule. The board did not become stochastic, so the run cannot answer the question it was written to ask, and E=0.765 vs 1.480 is not reported as a result. The cause is the CORPUS, not the policy: these testbenches are effective enough that 20k random vectors never change a verdict — true properties pass every time, the mutant is caught every time. Seed variation has nothing to act on.
revisit_if: a design/mutant pair enters the corpus whose bug random vectors genuinely sometimes miss — rare-corner, not directed
a testbench with constrained-random stimulus replaces the directed benches, which would make seeds matter by construction
complexity_note: THE DETERMINISM CAVEAT ON EXPERIMENTS 13 AND 14 THEREFORE STANDS, UNDISCHARGED. Their +20.0% and +22.2% remain exact arithmetic on deterministic boards rather than sampled estimates, and their noise criteria remain vacuous. Two defects were found building this: every obligation was initially a TRUE property, so the board could never have varied (fixed by adding the mutant-refuted mvf.bug, named explicitly in source); and per-obligation counters were initialised in attach_features rather than __init__, so any featureless worker crashed on its first simulation — latent for as long as every such experiment was formal-only. TEMPTING AND REFUSED: shrinking nvec until the mutant is sometimes missed would manufacture variance by tuning the instrument toward the desired result. If that is done it must be pre-registered with the vector count justified as realistic, not chosen because it produces noise.
